claim: Ours, from looking at the campaign's machine rooms: their detail is wall tiles with pipes and dials painted in, walls cut into panel and pilaster rhythm, hazard strips at openings, consoles let into a wall on a sill, faceted solids shaded facet by facet, and light pulsing on the machine, with almost no wall sprites; Gravesend's machine hall was built that way. A count once quoted (900 metal-walled sectors, 0.21 wall sprites per 10,000 of wall) has no tool that reproduces it.
evidence: E3M5 s138 (298:1536 115:256 298:1536), s158; E6M3 s150-157 and E3M5 s6 hazard strips; E3M6 s414-416 consoles; E3M5 s14 facets 4 -> 16 -> 4; E3M3 generator pulse wave 5, amplitude -32 (projects/blood-city/level/l3_shed.py)

Unsettled: a miner that names the campaign's metal-walled sectors by a stated tile set and counts wall sprites per length of their wall would make this a tendency; the 0.21/10,000 figure survives only in projects/blood-city/level/l3_shed.py's comment
use: Compose a machine hall from wall records cut into a rhythm of technical tiles; hang at most a few grates.
